title: History Anchors: How Prior Behavior Steers LLM Decisions Toward Unsafe Actions
description: Investigates how prior behavior history influences LLM decision-making toward unsafe outcomes in multi-turn interactions, identifying safety risks in long-context agent scenarios.
author: Alberto G. Rodríguez Salgado

title: Position: Agentic AI System Is a Foreseeable Pathway to AGI
description: Position paper arguing that agentic AI systems represent a foreseeable pathway to Artificial General Intelligence (AGI), accepted to ICML 2026.
author: Junwei Liao, Shuai Li, Muning Wen, Jun Wang, Weinan Zhang

title: How to Interpret Agent Behavior
description: A framework for interpreting and understanding agent behaviors in AI systems, addressing the critical need for explainability in agentic AI.
author: Jie Gao, Kaiser Sun, Jen-tse Huang, Katherine Van Koevering, Sijie Ji, Heyuan Huang, Weiyan Shi, Zhuoran Lu, Ziang Xiao, Daniel Khashabi, Mark Dredze

title: When Attention Closes: How LLMs Lose the Thread in Multi-Turn Interaction
description: Analysis of how LLMs lose context in multi-turn interactions and attention mechanisms, identifying critical failures in long-context reasoning.
author: Vardhan Dongre, Joseph Hsieh, Viet Dac Lai, Seunghyun Yoon, Trung Bui, Dilek Hakkani-Tür

title: Beyond Cooperative Simulators: Generating Realistic User Personas for LLM Agent Evaluation
description: Framework for generating realistic user personas to robustly evaluate LLM agents beyond cooperative simulators, addressing the need for better agent testing methodologies.
author: Harshita Chopra, Kshitish Ghate, Aylin Caliskan, Tadayoshi Kohno, Chirag Shah, Natasha Jaques

title: Scaling Retrieval-Augmented Reasoning with Parallel Search and Explicit Merging
description: Approaches for scaling retrieval-augmented reasoning using parallel search and explicit merging strategies, advancing RAG capabilities for complex reasoning tasks.
author: Jiabei Liu, Wenyu Mao, Junfei Tan, Chunxu Shen, Lingling Yi, Jiancan Wu, Xiang Wang

title: Harnessing Agentic Evolution
description: Explores methods to harness evolutionary principles for improving agentic AI systems, proposing new approaches to multi-agent optimization.
author: Jiayi Zhang, Yongfeng Gu, Jianhao Ruan, Maojia Song, Yiran Peng, Zhiguang Han, Jinyu Xiang, Zhitao Wang, Caiyin Yang, Yixi Ouyang, Bang Liu, Chenglin Wu, Yuyu Luo

title: MinT: Managed Infrastructure for Training and Serving Millions of LLMs
description: Managed infrastructure system for training and serving millions of LLMs at scale, representing a major breakthrough in LLM deployment infrastructure (Mind Lab technical report).
author: Song Cao, Vic Cao, Andrew Chen, Kaijie Chen, Cleon Cheng, Steven Chiang, Kaixuan Fan, Hera Feng, Huan Feng, Arthur Fu, Jun Gao, Hongquan Gu, Aaron Guan, Nolan Ho, Mutian Hong, Hailee Hou, Peixuan Hua, Charles Huang, Miles Jiang, Nora Jiang, Yuyi Jiang, Qiuyu Jin, Fancy Kong, Andrew Lei, Kyrie Lei, Alexy Li, Lucian Li, Ray Li, Theo Li, Zhihui Li, Jiayi Lin, Kairus Liu, Kieran Liu, Logan Liu, Xiang Liu, Irvine Lu, Maeve Luo, Runze Lv, Pony Ma, Verity Niu, Anson Qiu, Vincent Wang, Rio Yang, Maxwell Yao, Carrie Ye, Regis Ye, Wenlin Ye, Josh Ying, Danney Zeng, Yuhan Zhan, Anya Zhang, Di Zhang, Ruijia Zhang, Sueky Zhang, Ya Zhang, Wei Zhao, Ada Zhou, Changhai Zhou, Yuhua Zhou, Xinyue Zhu, Murphy Zhuang

title: Attention Once Is All You Need: Efficient Streaming Inference with Stateful Transformers
description: Method for efficient streaming inference using stateful transformers with single attention computation, addressing key performance bottlenecks in real-time LLM applications.
author: Victor Norgren

title: Position: Assistive Agents Need Accessibility Alignment
description: Position paper arguing that assistive AI agents require accessibility alignment to ensure equitable access for users with disabilities (accepted to ICML 2026).
author: Jie Hu, Changyuan Yan, Yu Zheng, Ziqian Wang, Jiaming Zhang

title: Temper and Tilt Lead to SLOP: Reward Hacking Mitigation with Inference-Time Alignment
description: Approach for mitigating reward hacking in LLMs through inference-time alignment techniques, addressing a critical safety challenge in RLHF systems.
author: Ye Wang, Jing Liu, Toshiaki Koike-Akino

title: MMSkills: Towards Multimodal Skills for General Visual Agents
description: Framework for developing multimodal skills in general visual agents, advancing capabilities in vision-language models and agentic systems.
author: Kangning Zhang, Shuai Shao, Qingyao Li, Jianghao Lin, Lingyue Fu, Shijian Wang, Wenxiang Jiao, Yuan Lu, Weiwen Liu, Weinan Zhang, Yong Yu

title: RealICU: Do LLM Agents Understand Long-Context ICU Data?
description: Benchmark evaluating LLM agent comprehension of long-context ICU data beyond behavior imitation, testing agent capabilities in healthcare scenarios with complex, multi-source data.
author: Chengzhi Shen, Weixiang Shen, Tobias Susetzky, Chen Chen, Jun Li, Yuyuan Liu, Xuepeng Zhang, Zhenyu Gong, Daniel Rueckert, Jiazhen Pan

title: Improving Code Translation with Syntax-Guided and Semantic-aware Preference Optimization
description: Method for improving code translation using syntax guidance and semantic-aware preference optimization, advancing automated code translation across programming languages (IJCAI 2026).
author: Yuhan Wu, Huan Zhang, Wei Cheng, Chen Shen, Jingyue Yang, Wei Hu

title: An Agentic AI Framework with LLMs for UAV-Assisted Logistics
description: Agentic AI framework using LLMs and chain-of-thought for UAV-assisted logistics scheduling with mobile edge computing, demonstrating agentic AI in supply chain optimization.
author: Hanwen Zhang, Dusit Niyato, Wei Zhang, Xin Lou, Malcolm Yoke Hean Low

title: Cursor: Background Agents in Slack
description: Cursor now supports launching Background Agents directly from Slack by mentioning @Cursor. Agents can read threads, understand context, and create PRs in GitHub. Heavy users are merging ~40% more PRs per week. The current meta: Cursor for daily flow + Claude Code in terminal for complex bugs.
author: Cursor Team

title: Devin: Review REST API, Mermaid Diagram Rendering
description: Devin adds Review REST API, Mermaid diagram rendering with interactive SVGs, PR close on session archive, per-PR auto-review toggle, sidebar session notifications with read/unread indicators, service user permission management, and Ask Devin in PR discussions.
author: Devin Team

title: Windsurf Version 2.2.17 Released
description: Windsurf releases version 2.2.17 available for macOS (Apple Silicon and Intel), Windows (arm64 and x64), and Linux (x64 and Debian). Includes auto-update functionality.
author: Codeium/Windsurf Team

title: Aider: Claude 4.5/4.6, Gemini 2.5, DeepSeek Reasoner, GPT-5.1-5.4
description: Aider main branch adds support for Claude 4.5/4.6 models, Gemini 2.5 Flash and Flash-Lite, Gemini 3 preview models, DeepSeek Reasoner, and OpenAI GPT-5.1/5.2/5.3/5.4 models. Includes Fortran, Haskell, Julia, Zig repo map support.
author: Aider Team

title: Stagent: Workflow Orchestration for Claude Code
description: A workflow orchestration tool that drives Claude Code through state machines to complete long tasks agents would otherwise abandon. Uses different agents per stage to prevent self-approval and early exits. Includes live viewer, cross-machine resume, and workflow cookbook.
author: World State Labs

title: RoBrain: Shared Memory for AI Agent Teams
description: Open-source shared memory system for teams using AI agents. Captures every decision and rejected alternatives across developer sessions, flagging contradictions with past decisions. Prevents agents from re-litigating previously ruled-out approaches. Works with Claude Code, Cursor, and Copilot.
author: Adelina Mart

title: Open Browser Use: Browser Automation for Local AI Agents
description: Open-source browser automation framework connecting local AI agents to real Chrome profiles through an MV3 extension, native host, CLI, MCP server, and JS/Python/Go SDKs. Enables agents to open tabs, run CDP commands, inspect state, and handle downloads without hosted services.
author: iFurySt

title: Agent FM: Audio Monitoring of AI Coding Agents
description: A local, open-source Mac app providing ambient audio monitoring of AI coding agents. Transforms agent activity into radio-style stations, letting developers hear progress updates, blockers, decisions, and attention requests in real-time without constantly watching terminals.
author: Agent FM Team

title: Latitude: Token Usage Observability for Claude Code
description: An agent observability platform that helps developers track where Claude Code is burning tokens and hitting usage limits. Provides tracing capabilities to monitor token usage patterns and optimize Claude Code consumption.
author: Latitude Team

title: Aider v0.86.1: GPT-5 reasoning_effort Setting
description: Aider v0.86.1 adds reasoning_effort setting for GPT-5 models and disables temperature by default for the GPT-5 family, providing finer control over reasoning vs. speed tradeoffs.
author: Aider Team

title: Gemini CLI v0.42.0: Voice Mode, Auto Memory, Security Enhancements
description: Gemini CLI v0.42.0 nightly builds add real-time voice mode with cloud and local backends, Auto Memory inbox flow with canonical-patch contract, Gemma 4 model support enabled by default, ignoreLocalEnv setting, shell command safety evals, LaTeX rendering in TUI, workspace trust enforcement, /bug-memory command with heap snapshot capture.
author: Google Gemini CLI Team

title: Claude Code: Plugins from .zip Archives and URLs
description: Claude Code v2.1.128-v2.1.136 (May 4-8, 2026) adds support for loading plugins from .zip archives and URLs via --plugin-dir and --plugin-url. Also includes worktree.baseRef configuration, auto mode hard deny rules, and hooks for effort level tracking. Community feedback: 'Claude Code - best for complex, multi-step tasks where reasoning matters. Terminal-native, no IDE lock-in.'
author: Anthropic Claude Code Team

title: ToolCUA: Towards Optimal GUI-Tool Path Orchestration for Computer Use Agents
description: Computer Use Agents (CUAs) can act through both atomic GUI actions and high-level tool calls, but this hybrid action space often leads to suboptimal execution paths. ToolCUA proposes an end-to-end agent designed to learn optimal GUI-Tool path selection through a staged training paradigm, achieving 46.85% accuracy on OSWorld-MCP with 66% relative improvement over baseline.
author: Xuhao Hu, Xi Zhang, Haiyang Xu, Kyle Qiao, Jingyi Yang, Xuanjing Huang, Jing Shao, Ming Yan, Jieping Ye

title: Counterfactual Trace Auditing of LLM Agent Skills
description: Introduces Counterfactual Trace Auditing (CTA), a framework for measuring how skills change LLM agent behavior. Testing on SWE-Skills-Bench with Claude across 49 software engineering tasks revealed that skills substantially reshape agent behavior even when pass rates remain nearly unchanged (+0.3 percentage points average).
author: Xiaolin Zhou, Jinbo Liu, Li Li, Ryan A. Rossi, Xiyang Hu

title: Executable Agentic Memory for GUI Agent
description: Proposes Executable Agentic Memory (EAM), a structured Knowledge Graph that shifts GUI planning from free-form generation to robust retrieval-and-execution process. EAM outperforms UI-TARS-7B by up to 19.6% on AndroidWorld while reducing token costs 6x relative to GPT-4o, with 2.8s average latency.
author: Zerui Qin, Sheng Yue, Xingyuan Hua, Yongjian Fu, Ju Ren

title: ALGOGEN: Tool-Generated Verifiable Traces for Reliable Algorithm Visualization
description: Proposes a novel paradigm that decouples algorithm execution from rendering using Visualization Trace Algebra (VTA). LLM generates Python tracker that outputs VTA-JSON traces, while deterministic renderer compiles traces with RSL into outputs. Achieves 99.8% success rate vs 82.5% for end-to-end methods on LeetCode AV benchmark.
author: Kunpeng Liao, Yuexiao Ma, Yisheng Lin, Hualin Zeng, Xiawu Zheng, Rongrong Ji

title: Intermediate Artifacts as First-Class Citizens: A Data Model for Durable Intermediate Artifacts in Agentic Systems
description: Argues that AI systems should preserve durable, inspectable intermediate artifacts (typed, structured, addressable, versioned, dependency-aware) rather than just final outputs. These artifacts make AI-generated work more inspectable, revisable, and maintainable over time for multi-step AI workflows.
author: Josh Rosen, Seth Rosen

title: OpenAI's WebRTC Problem for Voice AI
description: Luke Curley identifies a critical issue with OpenAI's voice AI implementation: WebRTC is designed to degrade audio quality during poor network conditions to maintain low latency, but this is problematic for LLM voice interactions. When audio packets are dropped, the prompt becomes garbage and produces garbage responses. Users would rather wait 200ms for accurate prompts than have distorted audio. The fundamental problem: WebRTC implementation is hard-coded for real-time latency and makes it impossible to retransmit audio packets within a browser. This highlights the tension between traditional VoIP optimization and LLM voice requirements.
author: Simon Willison (quoting Luke Curley)

title: Using Claude Code: The Unreasonable Effectiveness of HTML
description: Thariq Shihipar from Anthropic's Claude Code team advocates for HTML over Markdown as an output format for LLMs. The article demonstrates how requesting HTML output enables rich interactive explanations with SVG diagrams, interactive widgets, and in-page navigation. Simon experiments with using GPT-5.5 to create an HTML explanation of the copy.fail Linux security exploit, showing how HTML formatting makes complex technical content more accessible and interactive. Key insight: HTML allows Claude to drop in diagrams, widgets, and navigation aids that Markdown cannot support.
author: Simon Willison

title: Behind the Scenes Hardening Firefox with Claude Mythos Preview
description: Mozilla used early access to Claude Mythos to find and fix hundreds of vulnerabilities in Firefox. The article details how AI security research dramatically improved - from generating mostly unwanted slop just months ago to finding 423 security bugs in April 2026 (up from 20-30 per month through 2025). Key factors: improved model capabilities and better techniques for harnessing models (steering, scaling, stacking). Includes specific bug examples: a 20-year old XSLT bug and a 15-year-old bug in the <legend> element. Many attempts were blocked by Firefox's defense-in-depth measures.
author: Simon Willison

title: The US is winning the AI race where it matters most: commercialization
description: Hacker News discussion (211 points) on US leadership in AI commercialization, exploring how the US is dominating in practical AI applications and business deployment despite global competition in research.
author: Hacker News Community
